legend: Mesothelioma of epithelioid type, showing a small sheet of malignant mesothelial cells surrounded by lymphocytes and macrophages (pleural effusion, Giemsa).

Mesothelioma of epithelioid subtype. Minute tissue fragment of malignant mesothelial cells, with pink granular material in the background, suggestive of hyaluronan. Note the cytoplasmic blebs (pleural effusion, Giemsa).
Same patient as in Fig. <<#23652>>, 2 years later. Metastasis in the thoracic wall in a scar after thoracotomy (transbronchial FNAB, Giemsa).
Highly cellular direct smear showing plentiful variably sized, berry-like, 3D tissue fragments with scalloped borders (Giemsa).
Variably sized tissue fragments and spherical papillae with collagenous cores. Some of the spheres are hollow, surrounding a loose pink matrix, or show vacuolization of the cells (cell block, H&E).
Direct smear showing a complex papillary tissue fragment and other spherical papillae with epithelium surrounding a pink matrix (Pap).
Direct smear showing several large multinucleated mesothelioma cells with relatively dense cytoplasm and marked nuclear enlargement and pleomorphism (Pap).

Direct smear showing malignant mesothelial cells that vary in size from mildly enlarged to gigantic multinucleated cells, with dense squamoid cytoplasm with a frilly pale margin and marked nuclear pleomorphism (Pap).
Variably sized mesothelial cells, seen in small tissue fragments and as single cells, some gigantic in size and multinucleated (Pap).
Malignant mesothelial cells showing variable size and including pseudokeratotic cells with pyknotic nuclei and orangeophilic cytoplasm (liquid-based cytopathology, Pap).
Tissue fragments of mesothelioma showing the Oil Red O stain highlighting numerous perinuclear fat droplets in fresh smears.
Rounded, densely cellular, spherical tissue fragments floating in a mucin-like material representing the high background hyaluronan secreted by the malignant mesothelial cells (Pap).
Papillary tissue fragment with a collagen core and covered in an atypical mesothelial cell layer. Hyaluronan is present, appearing as granular ropy material in the background (cell block, H&E).
The malignant cells are primarily seen as a discohesive population of loosely attached or single cells, many of which have a frilly margin to the denser, more central cytoplasm (Pap).
Strong nuclear and cytoplasmic positivity for calretinin (cell block, ICC).
Pleural mesothelioma cells show loss of MTAP cytoplasmic expression (cell block, ICC).
Pleural mesothelioma showing cytoplasmic marginal D2-40 positivity (cell block, ICC).

Cohesive tissue fragment of mildly crowded malignant mesothelial cells with considerable cytoplasm (Pap). Inset: FISH of Pap-stained smear showing homozygous 9p21 deletion: increased copy numbers of chromosomes 3 (red), 7 (green), and 17 (blue), and complete loss of 9p21 (gold); benign reference cell with two intact 9p21 signals in the upper-right corner.
Tissue fragments of malignant mesothelial cells with intracytoplasmic lipid vacuoles (lipid-rich mesothelioma) (pleural effusion, Pap).
Tissue fragments of mesothelioma with intracytoplasmic lipid vacuoles in the abundant cytoplasm (pleural effusion, Giemsa).
Tissue fragment of mesothelioma with intracytoplasmic lipid vacuoles in the abundant cytoplasm (pleural effusion, Oil Red O).

> 90% of mesotheliomas express WT1

Some mesotheliomas express PAX8, especially in the peritoneum and in women {28877056; 32769428; 29241740}

Calretinin is expressed in as many as 30% of serous carcinomas of the ovary {16056246}
